name: Nuala Ní Dhomhnaill
text: Nuala Ní Dhomhnaill (1952– ) was a poet indexed by Koch under the headword Ní Dhomhnaill, Nuala. She was born in England to Irish-speaking parents. She spent part of her childhood with her mother's family in the West Kerry Gaeltacht. She graduated from University College Cork, where she belonged to the Innti writers' group. After seven years in her husband's native Turkey, she returned to Ireland (Éire) in 1979. She held a creative-writing bursary from the Irish Arts Council. Her poems won many prizes, including the O'Shaughnessy Award in 1988. She also won the America Ireland Fund's prize for literary work in 1991. In 1992 she was named the first writer in residence at University College Cork. She later held a visiting scholars post in Irish studies at Boston College and a fellowship at Villanova University. In 2001 she took the Ireland Chair of Poetry. She is a member of Aosdána, the Irish academy of artists. Though she writes in Irish, readers most often meet her work in translation, carried out by leading contemporary poets. Her best poems are consciously autobiographical. They identify with female figures from the folklore of Ireland and the wider mythology of East and West. This blend of voices produces an original and imaginative portrait of the female mind. Major collections include An Dealg Droighin (1981) and Pharaoh's Daughter (1990, translated by Carson).
